"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"Done talking." Gunther turns away. "Come back when you're not playing detective."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone? ...at least, that's how it looks to me."
"I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie."
"Still on needing to be alone."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Just my read."
"Kenneth always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sleep's gone strange. I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Nobody says Kenneth's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"This one — Brazil Nuts. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — American Ginseng. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. Kingston, Jamaica never taught me that. The treeline did."
"Still on how you slept."
"You want me to follow you into the dark? Earn that first."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Not that it matters."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
*Last time, they came at you for asking. That's not innocence talking. Hold your ground.*

"You take those walks that don't need to happen. Still breathing your own air?"

"Nobody's settled the ambush against me yet."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.

You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.

"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."

"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."

"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"This one — Field Mustard. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Papaya. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*You know the counter-attack now — the anger IS the tell. It means the accusation landed. Don't flinch.*
"I wasn't an ER nurse. I was a roofer. Sometimes I can hear it not being true while it's leaving my mouth. I say it anyway. It's like watching someone else talk."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that wound care."
"We went over this," Rafael says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Rafael rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."

"This one — Egusi Melon. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Physic Nut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
*They deflected you last time, and what you have hasn't grown since. One more thread before you speak, or they'll slip away again.*
"Oh." A long pause. "I didn't think it was anyone's. It's gone — I ate it days ago. I'm sorry."
"Water's almost gone — 2 liters. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 2 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
"Alright — I should get back to it."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."

lines: d9: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Kenneth Webb is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d9: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d9: 🕯️ Kenneth Webb is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d9: What Kenneth kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d9: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Yerkezhan blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d9: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d9: 📖 LEARNED: Engines (Level 1). Air, fuel, spark. Every dead engine is missing one of the three — diagnose in that order.
d9: 📖 LEARNED: Repair & Mending (Level 1). Look at what's broken before you touch it: find the failure point, not the symptom. Most breaks are one small thing.
d9: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d9: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Kenneth Webb, 9 days. The mantle passes to Yerkezhan Mukhametova.
d9: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Yerkezhan Mukhametova, 40 — a mechanic. Her hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d9: The fire knew Yerkezhan — solid ground, earned at this fire.
